text:
acme-sre: hitting you all — after the v2 model rollout (yesterday) our chat assistant started returning old onboarding copy for a subset of users. This looks like stale responses tied to customer-specific prefixes. Here's a minimal repro: we send the same prompt but get different behavior depending on user id.

acme-sre: request id: r-0a1b2c3d, time: 2026-03-15T09:12:23Z. payload: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model": "redwood-v2-chat",
  "input": "How do I set up SSO for my team?",
  "user": "org:acme:user:345",
  "prefix_namespace": "promo_2025"
}
```

acme-sre: response (truncated): 
```
{
  "id": "r-0a1b2c3d",
  "output": "Sure! Here’s the old onboarding blurb we used to run in 2024..."
}
```

sara: escalated to us, filing an internal ticket. Customer says this only started after we moved redwood-v2-chat to the new serving runtime; pre-rollout behavior matched expected copy. They suspect KV/prefix caching is returning stale cached completions.

max: thanks @sara — can you confirm whether the requests that return stale content share the same prefix_namespace value? if yes, can you paste two full request IDs (one returning expected new text, one returning old)?

acme-sre: yes, both requests use prefix_namespace=promo_2025. IDs: r-0a1b2c3d (stale), r-0b2c3d4e (fresh). I attached small logs — both were served from us-east-1 hosted endpoint.

lisa: pinging eng-runtime and prod-oncall. @ivan can you check whether the cache key composition changed in the rollout? there was a change earlier that included model version + user id + prefix hash, but the new runtime may have dropped model version in the key.

ivan: saw the deploy-bot message — rollout v2 at 2026-03-14 22:08 UTC (commit abcdef123). Looking at the diff, we did refactor cache key generation into a shared utility. I see this in the new code: `key = f"kv:{prefix}"` whereas old code used `kv:{model}:{user}:{prefix_hash}`. that would definitely increase collisions across model versions/users. digging.

max: wow — that sounds like a plausible root cause. if the new key is too coarse, different users can receive cached completions intended for another model/user/prefix combo. we need repro to be sure. @sara can you provide the raw request headers for r-0a1b2c3d and r-0b2c3d4e (especially x-request-id, x-prefix, x-model, x-user)?

acme-sre: pasted headers (redacted): 
```
r-0a1b2c3d: x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d; x-model: redwood-v2-chat; x-user: org:acme:user:345; x-prefix: promo_2025; x-prefetch: true
r-0b2c3d4e: x-request-id: r-0b2c3d4e; x-model: redwood-v2-chat; x-user: org:acme:user:789; x-prefix: promo_2025; x-prefetch: true
```

ivan: confirms — both requests had same x-prefix. with the changed key they'd collapse into same cache entry. I'm pulling the KV store check now.

ivan: running quick check on the cache host (us-east-kv-3): `redis-cli --raw HGETALL kv:promo_2025` returns a single entry with value that looks like an old completion blob stamped 2024-11-02. TTL is -1.

support-bot: incident-log created: INC-2026-1937 (possible kv key collision after runtime refactor).

prod-oncall: we should triage impact: is this only for prefix-based cached completions, or for all KV namespaces? Also, how many prefixes are affected? I can run a query to count keys: `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'kv:*' | wc -l` and `redis-cli --scan --pattern 'kv:promo_*' | wc -l`.

ivan: quick counts: total kv:* keys = 14,312; kv:promo_* = 24. promo_2025 shows 1 entry (the stale blob). however, because the new key omitted model/user, a single kv:promo_2025 is being used to serve many requests.

max: suggested mitigation steps: (1) temporary fix = flush affected prefix keys to force re-generation, (2) short-term patch = roll forward a key-version bit so new keys won't collide with old blobs, (3) long-term = add unit/regression tests to ensure key composition includes (model, user, prefix_hash) and alert on sudden collapse in key cardinality.

lisa: can we do a targeted flush for promo_2025 now? risk to live traffic? If TTLs are absent, flushing will force cold starts for those users but that's acceptable for a short window with customer consent.

acme-sre: we prefer targeted flush vs rollback. please proceed. they said tolerance for a short increase in latency.

ivan: performing targeted delete: `redis-cli DEL kv:promo_2025` -> returns 1. confirm no more entries for that key.

ivan: re-run repro for r-0a1b2c3d (server side): now response shows updated welcome copy. r-0b2c3d4e also shows updated. both return new text.

acme-sre: confirmed on our side — both requests now match expected copy. thanks, team. :tada:

max: created a quick patch branch that bumps cache key version by adding a prefix `v2:` to keys generated by the new runtime. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/482. going to coordinate a tiny hotfix release and a canary rollout to ensure no regression.

ivan: note for postmortem — root cause = refactor that consolidated key composition but inadvertently removed model and user components from composed KV key. failure mode = cold keys were replaced by a single entry per prefix_namespace, producing stale cross-user outputs. recommended postmortem sections: timeline, root cause, mitigation, tests, rollout checklist.

lisa: I'll schedule an incident review with eng-runtime, support, and SRE tomorrow. @prod-oncall please add follow-up tasks: high-priority tests + an alert when average key cardinality drops by >50% in a region.

support-bot: INC-2026-1937 updated: status -> mitigated.

acme-sre: thanks all — appreciate the quick response. keeping thread open until PR is merged and canary looks green.

max: merging the patch to hotfix branch now, will roll canary to 10% for us-east in 15m. I'll post results.

ivan: canary looks good after 30m (no stale hits on logs). will do a gradual rollout with 5–10m windows.

max: rollout completed and keys are now namespaced with `v2:`. adding regression test and alert in monitoring. closing: INC-2026-1937 -> resolved.

acme-sre: verified final state and closing on our side. thank you! :heart:

sara: thanks team — filed follow-up PM (PM-1241) to include this in the next release notes and update runbook.

lisa: excellent. moving to postmortem drafting.
